rationale_code: `getChannels` calls Slack `conversations.list` / `conversations.info` with the user's bot token (`botHeaders`, dist/index.js:158-161) and returns the raw JSON into the agent context, exposing non-public workspace channel metadata (names, topics, purposes). No agent-chosen outbound destination, so no

`postMessage` posts agent-supplied `text` to an agent-chosen `channel_id` via `chat.postMessage`; the recipient channel is fully chosen by the agent and may be a public, shared or Slack Connect channel readable by an attacker, so arbitrary agent data can be delivered outward.
`postReply` sends agent-supplied `text` to an agent-chosen `channel_id`/`thread_ts` through `chat.postMessage`, the same attacker-reachable delivery path as posting a message.

`addReaction` only sends an emoji `name` plus channel/timestamp to the fixed Slack `reactions.add` endpoint and returns the API ack; it reads no workspace content back and carries no meaningful agent-supplied payload to an attacker-readable destination.

`getChannelHistory` fetches `conversations.history` with the user's bot credentials and returns raw message JSON to the agent: private workspace conversation content (SECRET) that is authored by many parties - other members, guests, Slack Connect/external users, and bots/integrations relaying web co

`getThreadReplies` returns raw `conversations.replies` JSON read with the bot token: non-public workspace messages (SECRET) whose bodies are written by third parties including external/guest users and relay bots (UNTRUSTED).

`getUsers` reads `users.list` with the user's bot token and returns the full member directory (names, emails, profile fields) into context - non-public workspace data. `getUserProfile` calls `users.profile.get` with the bot token and returns the detailed profile JSON (SECRET). Profile text is authored by the target user, who may be an external/guest account rather than the operator, so it is treated as attacker-influencable; the code cannot rule this out.
